author: charlespips
text:
Hi PS,

I'm also learning about PAZ for the past few days. Can I study together with you? Let's master this baby together shall we?

Here is what I've found when digging on PAZ... I've been thinking that each PAZ can containing one or more other PAZ (e.g. CP PAZ), and when drilling down to lower TF, there should be many more of them.

FTR PAZ is much bigger than CP PAZ, because I often found one or two CPPAZ inside one FTR PAZ (PAZ between two FTRs) of current time frame. I haven't dig deeper into lower TF for now, just this current TF (e.g. H1)

As you may have notice, most CP PAZ will create a long Momo candle (liquidity gaps) when engulfed, because the S/D has been compressed & gone. So, this automatically turning most momo candle as the valid PAZ as well. You know, price engulf, RT and head for the other edge of the engulf and flagging again to test the level. This might be (i'm not so sure yet) also the reason why IF is drawing Pole as his PAZ.

Next, PAZ when engulfed is gone, creating whole new set of PAZ at the top and the bottom of the flag after the engulf stop and ftr. So I guess this will answer Bobyv87's question.

now, what's puzzling me right now is how these PAZs interacting with each other, when there are one or more mini PAZ inside the big PAZ? what's the key to really capture this elephant in the chart (IF said PAZ is an elephant. You see it or you are not!

Should the zone really measured to the Pixel, or it can be a box like the one I asked in IF's journal, which crossing half-way of many tops and bottoms, looking at the SR flip which confirmed by Michal (I still have no idea what you guys are talking about in that thread.

)

What do you think, PS? kindly correct me if you have a different discovery.

CP

author: projectsagana
text:
I finally have my own personal written trading plan on hard copy. It's meant to be simple and will be editing it through out my learning curve to see what works and what doesn't.

It's Raining Money Trading Plan

[/size]

I. Easy As 1-2-3 Plan 1. Identify Location of price 2. Identify Direction of price 3. Identify Entry in price

II. Four Locations of Price 1. Inside/Reaction of a SUPPLY level

- The direction of price is currently up, and here is where we will WAIT for

signals whether price will bounce down or engulf the level up

2. Inside/Reaction of a DEMAND level

- The direction of price is currently down, and here is where we will WAIT for

signals whether price will bounce up or engulf the level down

3. After an ENGULF of a resistance or supply level

- An engulfing of a supply level into a PAZ means price most likely wants to go

to the next higher level of supply and here is where we WAIT for signals whether price indeed wants to keep going up or it was a FO

4. After an ENGULF of a support or demand level

- An engulf of a demand level into a PAZ means price most likely wants to go

the next lower level of demand and here is where we will WAIT for signals whether price indeed wants to keep going down or it was a FO

III. Money Map Guide 1. HTF vs LTF - HTFs will be used for identifying location and direction of price. LTFs will be used for entry in price

Style of Trading: HTF/LTF

A. Position: Monthly as HTF, and Daily as LTF *B. Swing: Wkly as HTF, and 4h as LTF *C. "Intra-Swing": 4h as HTF, and 15m as LTF D. Daily: 60m as HTF, and 15m as LTF

*I will be using Swing and "Intra-Swing" Style of Trading

- HTF is ALWAYS more significant than LTF - HTF supply would most likely end LTF uptrends - HTF demand would most likely end LTF downtrends - LTF uptrends would most likely end at HTF supply - LTF downtrends would most likely end at HTF demand - AT ALL TIMES, ALWAYS BE AWARE OF WHERE PRICE IS IN THE HTF

2. Engulf to PAZ

- When price engulfs a level into a PAZ, it would most likely reach the next

opposing level

- When price engulfs a supply level into a PAZ, it would most likely reach the

next higher level of supply

- When price engulfs a demand level into a PAZ, it would most likely reach the

next lower level of demand

Engulf of SUPPLY into PAZ simplified illustration

Engulf of DEMAND into PAZ simplified illustration

IV. The "Make Me Rich" Set Ups

- The most important, must have signal of all of the Make Me Rich Set Ups is:

Engulf

- No Engulf = NO Trade. ALWAYS WAIT FOR THE ALL MIGHTY ENGULF!! - Minimum potential RR is 3:1, if RR is 3:1, take profit at 2.5 RR, if RR is 4:1,

take profit at 3.5 RR

- Always have a stop loss pre-determined when entering a trade - Always have a profit target pre-determined when entering a trade - Risk per Trade: 1% of account balance

1. Reversal FL/FTR Demand

2. Reversal FL/FTR Supply

3. Reversal Bullish QM

4. Reversal Bearish QM

V. Profit and Risk Management

Risk Per Trade: 1% of account balance Position Size Calculator: www.babypips.com/tools/forex-

calculators/positionsize.php

Target per Trade: Minimum of 3-to-1 potential RR Monthly Target: 8% of account balance Maximum Loss per Week: 4% Maximum Open Trades Simultaneously: 4 Trades

1st Edition: 2-16-15

From here I will be forward testing it by trading live on a demo account. The only way for me to graduate from a demo trader to a live trader is if I manage to get 8% increase for 3 consecutive months.

At the same time I am demo trading, I will also be using FX Tester 2 to help me more about my rules
